name: Kaskor ASR
oneLiner: Khmer speech-to-text on a fine-tuned Whisper-small — best checkpoint 17.48% CER (self-reported) — public training and evaluation code, released weights, and an installable CLI.
seoDescription: Khmer speech-to-text fine-tuning on Whisper-small — best checkpoint self-reports 17.48% CER on its own held-out split — from raw audio to a pip-installable CLI.
question: Can a fully public fine-tuning pipeline — code, splits, and released weights — make Khmer speech recognition approachable with limited public data?
problem: Khmer speech interfaces are held back by low-resource data, evaluation that standard word-based metrics get wrong, and research pipelines that nobody else can rerun. Most Khmer ASR work is not reproducible by a second person, which makes results hard to trust and harder to build on.
targetUsers: Developers and researchers who need Khmer speech-to-text building blocks, and — eventually — voice-first products for Khmer speakers, starting with agricultural data intake where typing is impractical.
whyItMatters: Speech is the natural interface for many Khmer-speaking users, especially in field contexts. Because the training and evaluation code is public, every future improvement in data or compute can translate into a better model instead of a new unverifiable claim — even though the raw audio itself stays private.
exactRole: Sole builder of the public pipeline: data preparation, training and evaluation scripts, CLI packaging, and documentation.
research: Studied why word error rate misleads for Khmer — the script does not separate words with spaces, so WER punishes segmentation choices rather than recognition quality. Character error rate became the primary metric, with WER kept only as a secondary signal, and the reasoning is documented in the repository.
validation: Evaluation runs on a held-out split through the repository's own evaluation script. There is no external benchmark or third-party validation yet — the published numbers are self-reported and the README says so.
proposedSolution: One repository that packages the entire path from raw Khmer audio to a trained, exportable model: dataset inspection, manifest building, resampling, speaker-stratified splitting, feature caching, training, evaluation, export, and a pip-installable transcription CLI for files, folders, and microphone input.
userWorkflow: Inspect the raw audio dataset and build CSV manifests
Resample audio to 16 kHz and verify formats so preprocessing cannot hide evaluation differences
Evaluate with CER as the primary metric on the held-out split
Export the model and transcribe through the CLI
systemArchitecture: A staged pipeline of eleven Python scripts with explicit inputs and outputs. Raw audio stays outside git by design; the versioned repository holds manifests, scripts, and evaluation logic, and the fine-tuned weights are published separately on Hugging Face — so both the recipe and the resulting model are public even where the audio cannot be.
methods: Fine-tuning openai/whisper-small with Hugging Face Transformers, torchaudio preprocessing, speaker-stratified splits, feature caching for iteration speed, and CER-first evaluation chosen for the linguistics of Khmer script.
businessValue: An enabling layer rather than a product: reliable Khmer speech-to-text lowers the cost of every voice-first product idea that follows, including agricultural data intake for the Chomkar direction. Framed as potential — no commercial use exists yet.
contractsPolicy: The code is MIT-licensed and public, and the fine-tuned weights are published on Hugging Face. The real commercial-legal question is dataset rights: audio provenance, speaker consent, and licensing must be documented before the raw audio or any dataset is released — which is why the recordings themselves stay private.
dataPrivacy: Voice recordings are personal data. Raw audio is excluded from the repository, and any future release of weights or datasets requires documented consent and a provenance review first.
risks: A single aggregate metric can overstate quality for underrepresented speakers, dialects, or noisy environments
Published numbers could be mistaken for production-grade accuracy claims
Voice data misuse — any future dataset release without consent review would harm real speakers
humanApprovalPoints: Publishing model weights or any dataset
Making any public accuracy claim beyond the self-reported repository numbers
Using recorded voices in a real product
technicalDecisions: Character error rate as the primary metric, because Khmer does not reliably separate words with spaces
Raw audio stays outside git; manifests, scripts, and evaluation logic are versioned, and the fine-tuned weights are released on Hugging Face
The full training pipeline is separate from the lightweight CLI that transcription users install
Text normalization and 16 kHz verification happen explicitly, so evaluation differences cannot hide inside preprocessing

completedWork.text: Eleven-script pipeline covering inspection, manifests, resampling, splitting, caching, training, evaluation, export, and Hub push
Pip-installable CLI supporting files, folders, reference text, and optional microphone input
Fine-tuned model weights (v0.0) published on Hugging Face with processor configs and a transcription script
Speaker-stratified train/val/test manifests committed to the repository
Model card with dataset composition and known failure modes

evidence.text: The public repository contains the full training pipeline — real code, not documentation of intent (train.py, run_eval.py, and nine supporting scripts).
Committed CSV manifests (a 33.6 MB training manifest plus validation and test splits) corroborate a substantial dataset behind the training work.
Training used approximately 86,500 audio samples — the committed train.csv manifest lists them row by row, alongside ~4,800-sample validation and test manifests.

results.text: Best checkpoint self-reports 17.48% CER, 67.2% WER (secondary), and 0.0346 evaluation loss on the project's own held-out split — measured by the repository's evaluation script. The fine-tuned weights (v0.0) are public on Hugging Face; the raw audio remains private, so training-from-scratch reproduction still requires the source recordings.
No third-party or benchmark validation exists yet; the model is early (self-labeled v0.0) and not production-grade transcription for every Khmer speaker or environment.

constraints: Limited public Khmer speech data; reproducing training requires access to the source audio and suitable compute
Raw audio cannot be responsibly published until dataset provenance and consent are documented
Evaluation is a single held-out split, not per-condition analysis
tradeoffs: Whisper-small over larger models, trading headline accuracy for iteration speed on available compute
Audio stays out of git; the weights live on Hugging Face, so running inference means installing the CLI and pulling the v0.0 checkpoint

lessonsLearned: Metric choice is a linguistic decision before it is a technical one — CER vs WER changes what 'better' means for Khmer
Normalization and resampling silently distort evaluation unless they are explicit, versioned steps
Reproducibility discipline (manifests, splits, scripts in git) is what turns a personal experiment into something others can build on
nextValidation: Evaluate by speaker, province, recording device, and noise condition
Publish a model card with dataset composition and known failure modes
Measure latency and accuracy inside a real voice-first product workflow

aiAssistance.scope: Claude assisted with script scaffolding, refactoring, and documentation drafts.
